      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Your liver is the largest organ inside your body. It helps your body digest food, store energy, and remove poisons. Primary liver <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">cancer</span></span> starts in the liver.  Metastatic liver <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">cancer</span></span> starts somewhere else and spreads to your liver. </p><p>Risk factors for primary liver <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">cancer</span></span> include :</p><ul><li>Having hepatitis B or C</li><li>Heavy alcohol use</li><li>Having cirrhosis, or scarring of the liver</li><li>Having hemochromatosis, an iron storage disease</li><li>Obesity and diabetes</li></ul><p>Symptoms can include a lump or pain on the right side of your abdomen and yellowing of the skin. However, you may not have symptoms until the <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">cancer</span></span> is advanced.  This makes it harder to treat. Doctors use tests that examine the liver and the blood to diagnose liver <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">cancer</span></span>. Treatment options include surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, or liver transplantation. </p><p>NIH: National <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">Cancer</span></span> Institute</p></content>
